title: A scarce nesting site
hook: Compare the effects on both participants.

knows: Ecological interactions can affect participants differently.
doesNotKnow: Both competitors experience a cost relative to the stated uncontested baseline. The interaction is competition.

misconception: An interaction must affect both participants in the same way.
objective: Classify the stated effects of an ecological interaction.

claims.text: Question, diagram and reveal: Two birds compete for scarce nesting sites, reducing each bird's expected success compared with having the site uncontested. Using + for benefit, − for harm and 0 for no appreciable effect, which signs describe Bird A and Bird B, in that order? Bird A: −; Bird B: −. Both competitors experience a cost relative to the stated uncontested baseline. The interaction is competition.
claims.source: Stipulated simplified example; ecological definitions: OpenStax https://openstax.org/books/biology-2e/pages/45-6-community-ecology

claims.text: Icons and signs summarize the stipulated interaction and do not quantify fitness or capture every ecological effect.
Recall: What term describes the Bird A–Bird B interaction as stated in the lesson? Both competitors experience a cost relative to the stated uncontested baseline. The interaction is competition.
